objectives: Understand how eddy currents occur, with diagrams, and state their practical applications.
Understand how self-induction occurs, and define the self-inductance (L).

content.label: 📌 3-4 Eddy Currents
content.html: In many electrical devices (such as measuring instruments, motors, vehicles, metal detectors, and the brakes of some heavy wheels) we find a metal body moving in a magnetic field that changes with time. According to Faraday's law of induction, the changing magnetic field generates induced currents in the metal body, in a direction perpendicular to that magnetic flux, as shown in figure (3-5a). These induced currents are called eddy currents, because they circulate in closed paths within the conducting body, resembling the currents generated in water as concentric circles. These induced currents cause a heat loss according to Joule's law, heating up electrical devices — one of the harmful effects of eddy currents.

content.svgAriaLabel: Simulation of eddy currents and the opposing force as a metal plate moves under a magnet
content.sectionHeading: 🕹️ Interactive Simulation: The Force Opposing Eddy Currents (Figure 3-6)
content.descriptionHtml: When a metal plate moves beneath a magnetic pole, eddy currents are generated at the two edges of the region affected by the field (entering and leaving), and by Lenz's law these induced eddy currents generate a force that opposes the plate's motion (a retarding force); this is the basis for the operation of eddy-current brakes used in some heavy wheels.

ruleBoxes.html: The plate is at rest: no change in flux, and no eddy currents.

labels.statusMoving: The plate is moving: eddy currents are generated at the two edges of the magnet, producing a force that opposes the plate's motion (Lenz's law) — the basis of eddy-current brakes.
labels.statusAtRest: The plate is at rest: no change in magnetic flux, no eddy currents, and no opposing force.

content.label: 📌 3-5 Self-Induction
content.html: Faraday's law states that any change in the magnetic flux through a coil induces an electromotive force in the coil, which causes an induced current to flow, which in turn generates an opposing magnetic field. Accordingly, a change in the current flowing through the coil leads to a change in the flux passing through it, and whenever the current changes, an induced electromotive force is self-generated in the coil for as long as the change continues.

items: The current flowing in the circuit increases with time.
The magnetic flux through the circuit increases as a result of the increasing current.
The increasing flux causes an electromotive force to be generated in the circuit that opposes the increase in magnetic flux (by Lenz's law).

content.html: This electromotive force generated in the circuit acts to oppose the direction of the original current, and it results from the increase in magnetic flux due to the increasing current when the switch is closed. This effect in the circuit is known as self-induction. content.html: Here (L) is the proportionality constant, called the self-inductance, and it depends on the coil's geometric shape, the material of the coil's core, its length, the area of a single turn, and its number of turns; its unit is the henry (H).

questions.question: Eddy currents are:
options: Steady currents that flow in straight wires
Induced currents that circulate in closed paths within a conducting body moving in a changing magnetic field
Currents produced only by batteries
Currents unrelated to the magnetic field
questions.explain: Eddy currents are induced currents that circulate in closed paths within a conducting body moving in a changing magnetic field.

questions.question: To reduce heat loss due to eddy currents in transformers, the metal core is made from:
options: Thin metal sheets insulated from one another
A single large solid metal piece
A material that is a perfect electrical insulator
A single thick copper wire
questions.explain: Using thin sheets insulated from one another reduces the size of the eddy-current loops, reducing heat loss.

questions.question: Self-induction is an effect that results from:
options: The presence of electrical resistance in the circuit alone
The presence of a high-voltage battery
A change in the current in the coil itself, generating an opposing electromotive force in it
The coil rotating about its own axis alone
questions.explain: Self-induction: a change in the current flowing through the coil generates an induced electromotive force in it that opposes this change.

questions.question: The unit of self-inductance (L) is:
options: The volt (V)
The ohm (Ω)
The weber (Wb)
The henry (H)
questions.explain: The unit of self-inductance is the henry (H).

questions.question: The self-inductance of a coil depends on:
options: The color of the coil's wire alone
The coil's geometric shape, its core material, its length, the area of a turn, and its number of turns
The surrounding room temperature alone
The price of the material the coil is made from
questions.explain: The self-inductance depends on the coil's geometric shape, its core material, its length, the area of a single turn, and its number of turns.

summary.heading: 📋 Lesson Summary
items: Eddy currents: induced currents that circulate in closed paths within a conducting body moving in a changing field, causing heat loss.
Metal bodies are made from thin insulated sheets to reduce eddy currents (as in transformers).
Self-induction: a change in the current in a coil generates an opposing electromotive force in it, \(\varepsilon_{ind}=-L\Delta I/\Delta t\).
Self-inductance \(L=N\Delta\varnothing/\Delta I\), with its unit the henry (H).
